document.cue: Describe a trip that you enjoyed.

text: I'd like to tell you about a trip to Charyn Canyon that I took with three university friends last summer. It's roughly two hundred kilometres from where we live, so we rented a car and set off at six in the morning to avoid the heat.

The drive itself was part of the fun, as the road winds through open steppe with mountains in the distance. When we arrived, we hiked down into the Valley of Castles, where the red rock formations look like ancient fortresses carved by the wind. We spent about three hours walking along the river at the bottom, taking photos and occasionally stopping to dip our feet in the freezing water. Since we hadn't booked a tour, we simply followed a narrow path and discovered a quiet spot where we had a picnic, with nobody else around. On the way back, our car broke down for a while, but a friendly local driver stopped and helped us fix it.

I enjoyed this trip so much because it was completely different from my everyday life. Normally I'm stuck in front of a screen, so being surrounded by such enormous, silent landscapes felt incredibly refreshing. It also strengthened my friendships, since we had to rely on one another when things went wrong. Looking back, the minor breakdown became the funniest part of the story, and we still laugh about it. It made me realise that you don't have to travel abroad to see something spectacular.
